title: Workflow question: Local AI with project context
author: Neither-Upstairs
selftext: I need help figuring out what a local AI game dev workflow might look like. My goal is to work in a completely isolated local setup where I can use a local model to communicate with a game engine like Unity or Godot. I’ve been trying to do research on this topic, but it seems like there’s not a lot of straightforward answers on getting this workflow set up completely. I’ve talked to Google Gemini and it hallucinates a lot and keeps talking me in circles and having me install things I don’t need. I understand that this is very hardware specific so there’s no cut and dry answer or catch all solution. Has anybody been able to successfully accomplish this workflow? If so, can someone point me in the right direction on how to set this up? An example of what I’m thinking of a workflow might look like would be a chat window where I can ask the AI to write a player movement script for me, then the AI would be able to see the open editor and understand the project before giving me an answer that works for the project. The biggest hurdle I’ve faced so far is getting a model to understand my local project and using that in context. Oh and don’t get me started on skills, I know that’s another beast that I haven’t been able to figure out yet with this. Thanks in advance!

comments.author: Hinnif
comments.body:
I really like CLI Opencode with LM Studio running as a server.

Setup LM Studio with a model of your choice, VRAM very important here. It's better to pick a smaller model and give it as much context room as you can in my experience.

Turn on the LM Studio server.

Configure opencode as here: https://opencode.ai/docs/config/

Then go to your project folder and open in terminal, run opencode and start agentically coding locally! Godot with the plugin "Godot AI" mcp servers works for me.

replies.author: Neither-Upstairs
replies.body: Gotcha, could you give me an example of how you work with this agent and what it does inside of your godot project?

replies.author: Hinnif
replies.body:
It will with guidance build game components. With the mcp servers I mentioned it can write game code, run headless tests and also run the game and take screenshots for testing. 

You do bump up against context limitations though, for large projects it is better to give it very directed briefs for specific tasks. You'll have to do a good job of understanding the code base yourself so you can act as the intelligent director.

I know it's not quite what you are after but for me where it has become really useful is in combination with a paid Claude pro subscription to save tokens.

I run the claude cli in the same project folder with te
the same mcp access and tell it that it can run opencode cli to direct tasks to my local model. The local model then has small well briefed tasks that it executes really well and cheaply. The calling Claude session waits for local model to finish a task and then checks output and debugs if required. In this workflow you can rely on claude keeping track of the core codebase better than a local model could.

replies.author: Neither-Upstairs
replies.body: Ah I see so you’re basically just using your local model as a grunt worker while your paid Claude sub manages the orchestration of it. Yeah that’s not exactly what I’m looking for but thanks for the info!

replies.author: Hinnif
replies.body:
I've done both. What I'm getting at is that when you are using local only, you've got to be all over the structure of your game yourself. The local model doesn't have the context length to do that for you.

You can use the local only workflow to build the game one small component at a time, but don't expect miracles!

replies.author: Neither-Upstairs
replies.body: Yeah, that makes a ton of sense. That’s basically how I have my actual job set up too I use Claude code through my job’s enterprise subscription and I just chat to it through VS code and it just manages the files and writes the code for me. But I don’t give it a huge monolithic prompts. I give it very targeted specific changes and it does it for me and the reason I can do that is because I understand how the code works under the hood so I know how to ask it to do tasks.

comments.author: novokvest
comments.body: I'm also very curious on this one. But I'm rather skeptical it can achieve anything valuable as I've tried simple text local LLM chats in the past and it is hundred times worse than any free api based chat like google AI or deepseek. If anyone managed to replicate some gamedev vibecoding local workflow on a consumer gpu please share your experience, video would be even better!

comments.author: AlgaeNo3373
comments.body: r/localllm might also have a good sense of it if you described workflows, they could suggest models etc according. to your setup? What rig you've got available might change what's possible.

replies.body: Yeah I should cross post this over there but I thought it was so niche to this field that I posted here first. I only have an RTX 3060 unfortunately, but looking to upgrade or get a gaming laptop to get more out of this workflow.
